sections.h2: Where is New Windsor and how is the town laid out?
sections.html:
New Windsor is a town in eastern Orange County, on the Hudson's west shore and directly below the city of Newburgh. Dutchess County lies across the river. The town spans 34.08 square miles of land, and the town sits at an elevation of 512 feet.

It is a patchwork of hamlets rather than one village. Vails Gate sits at an old crossroads just south of the city of Newburgh, Rock Tavern and Little Britain lie along Route 207 in the west, and Beaver Dam Lake and Firthcliffe Heights are near the southern line. Rock Tavern and Vails Gate each have their own ZIP code. Plum Point, on the river, became a park in 1996.

The 2020 census counted 27,805 people and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 27,844. That is a gain of just 0.1 percent, so you are selling into a settled suburb.

sections.h2: What is New Windsor's history, and does it affect homes today?
sections.html:
The General Assembly of New York founded the town on April 5, 1763. Scottish colonists had settled near Moodna Creek in 1685, and the name comes from Windsor, England.

The best-known chapter came in October 1782, when the Continental Army built a cantonment of more than 700 huts across about 1,600 acres, housing 6,000 to 8,000 soldiers, women and children. The town later bought a 167-acre tract covering much of the old hut sites. The National Purple Heart Hall of Honor stands on Route 300, a reminder that the Purple Heart traces back to Washington's Badge of Military Merit.

Older neighborhoods keep traces of that past. Clancyville, also called Ducktown, grew in the late 1800s around mills on Quassaick Creek, and the immigrant families who built small homes there enlarged them as they prospered. Additions made over generations are a common source of permit questions, so pull your paperwork before listing.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about homes and households in New Windsor?
sections.html:
Owners live in 73.2 percent of New Windsor homes, and the 2020 to 2024 survey puts the median home value at $371,900 against a typical monthly rent of $1,606. That is a long way below New Rochelle's $702,500 median value.

  • 10,981 households averaging 2.50 people
  • Median household income of $95,071 in 2024 dollars
  • Poverty rate of 5.4 percent
  • Adults 25 and older with a four-year degree: 37.3 percent
  • Average commute of 37.3 minutes one way

The commute is longer than in New Rochelle, which fits a town whose main road links are the Thruway and state routes. The 2022 business figures list $317,652,000 in retail sales, $172,823,000 in health care and social assistance revenue and $138,948,000 in transportation and warehousing revenue.

sections.h2: Which older properties and landmarks does the town point to?
sections.html:
Several stone houses from the 1700s survive. The Thomas McDowell House on Lake Road in Little Britain, built around 1770, was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2004, and the Squire Patton House dates from the 1790s. Knox's Headquarters at Vails Gate served as a Continental Army headquarters during the Revolution, and the state operates the New Windsor Cantonment State Historic Site.

Anyone selling a very old farmhouse near these landmarks should ask the town building department about historic or zoning limits before planning repairs. Churches add to the picture too: the Vails Gate United Methodist Church, founded in 1789, was the first Methodist church built in Orange County.

sections.h2: Which school district serves a house in New Windsor?
sections.html:
Four districts reach into the town: Newburgh City, Washingtonville Central, Cornwall Central and Valley Central, which is based in Montgomery. The answer depends on the street, so check by address instead of assuming.

The district also determines the school tax bill a new owner receives. Public schools inside the town include New Windsor School, Temple Hill School, Vails Gate High Technology Magnet School and Little Britain Elementary School.

Write the district name for your house into the paperwork you give the buyer, so nobody has to guess later.

sections.h2: How do the Thruway and Stewart Airport shape a sale?
sections.html:
The New York State Thruway, I-87, crosses the town north to south, and Route 207 is the main east-west state road. Stewart International Airport lies partly in New Windsor and partly in the town of Newburgh, and a newer entrance on Route 747 links it directly to the interstates.

Stewart began as an Air Force base. It now hosts the New York Air National Guard and a Marine Corps Reserve detachment. More than 8,000 acres of buffer land were acquired around the field when a larger jetport was planned, and many early farms were lost in the process.

Climate is humid continental with four distinct seasons, so roof condition and heating systems deserve attention in your pre-listing walk-through.

sections.h2: What does a late property tax payment cost in New Windsor?
sections.html:
Property tax bills are mailed in the last week of December and carry no penalty if paid in January. After that the Receiver of Taxes applies the charges shown below, and bills still unpaid after April 1 go to the county.

Payment monthCharge from the Town of New Windsor
JanuaryNo penalty
February1 percent
MarchAnother 1 percent, plus a $2.00 notice fee
After April 1Unpaid bills go to the Orange County Commissioner of Finance

Source: Town of New Windsor Receiver of Taxes page.

The town warns that a USPS postmark now shows the day mail is processed, which can be later than the day it is dropped off, and that a postage-meter mark does not count. The town lists these ways to make sure a payment counts as on time:

  • Ask for a hand-stamped postmark at the Post Office counter
  • Mail the check well before the due date
  • Pay in person at the Receiver of Taxes office
  • Pay online by e-check

If a bank holds your escrow, the bill goes to the bank, and anyone who refinanced or paid off a loan should tell the Receiver so the next bill reaches the right person.

sections.h2: Who handles STAR, permits and the deed?
sections.html:
The Assessor deals with exemptions, and the Building Department deals with permits. In August 2025 the Assessor posted a notice: owners who age into Enhanced STAR, or who have an ownership change, no longer file with the assessor. The state tells local assessors instead, and an ownership change is reported through the Homeowner Benefit Portal at the NYS Tax Department.

The Building Department enforces the New York State Uniform Fire Prevention and Building Code and the town's zoning law. Its permit list covers building permits, decks, pools and backflow preventers. If you added a deck or pool, ask for the permit and inspection record before you list.

The Orange County Clerk records the deed. The clerk's website says a copy of your deed costs about $5 straight from the office, and a free alert service notifies you when a deed or mortgage is recorded in your name, a guard against deed fraud. State rules put the TP-584 return with the county clerk, with payment due within 15 days of the deed's delivery.

faqs.q: Is New Windsor a town or a city?
faqs.a: A town in Orange County. The separate city of Newburgh runs along part of its northern line, and the Newburgh City School District covers sections of New Windsor.

faqs.q: What does a late New Windsor tax payment cost?
faqs.a: One percent in February, then a further one percent and a $2.00 notice fee in March. After April 1, unpaid bills go to the Orange County Commissioner of Finance.

faqs.q: How many school districts serve New Windsor?
faqs.a: Four: Newburgh, Washingtonville, Cornwall and Valley Central. Your address decides which one applies.

faqs.q: Who records a New Windsor deed?
faqs.a: The Orange County Clerk, not Town Hall. The TP-584 transfer tax form goes with the deed, and payment is due within 15 days after delivery.

faqs.q: What is the state transfer tax on a New Windsor home?
faqs.a: Two dollars per $500 of the price, charged to the seller unless the contract shifts it. The buyer's 1 percent mansion tax starts only at $1 million.
